#### `On`

```java
public final class On
```

Exports a static method as an event handler, one annotation per kind: the Java face of the Rust SDK's
`event!`. The processor generates the export that decodes the event into the method's parameters
and the `__udf_sig_<name>` export reading `event <kind>/1 ...`, which `event-set`
checks before binding. The parameter types are part of the kind, so a handler with another signature
does not compile. A handler answers with the `Events` or `Conflict` methods and returns
what they return (the status); an exception fails the call with its message.
```text
@On.BeforeWrite("guard_account")
static int guardAccount(EventRecord before, EventRecord after, Events.WriteInfo write) {
...
return Events.accept();
}
@On.XdrMerge("merge_counter")
static int mergeCounter(EventRecord current, EventRecord incoming, Conflict conflict) {
...
return Conflict.record(out, -1);
}
```
Every kind also takes the raw form `int name(int args, int argc)`, exported as it is with only
the signature generated. The name is the method's when the annotation's value is empty.

#### `Conflict`

```java
public final class Conflict
```

What an `xdr-merge` event is about: the current record (`local`, read by index 0), the
incoming XDR write (`remote`, index 1), and the description. A handler must be pure and
convergent: both data centres merge the same pair with the sides swapped and must land on the same record.
`remoteNewer` orders a bin's two sides by its own LUT and then source id, which is symmetric;
"mine first" is not.

methods deliver the verdict. The signature `signature` gives goes under `__udf_sig_<name>`.
